svg.title: CCD-Bench cultural-cluster choice behavior, not accuracy
svg.desc: Main CCD result. Model-line by cultural-cluster heatmap for CCD-Bench. Each cell shows percentage-point deviation from a 10% uniform baseline among valid visible selections only. Positive cells indicate the line selected that canonical cluster more often than uniform choice; negative cells indicate under-indexing. This is a choice-distribution result, not scalar accuracy.
svg.text: CCD-Bench cultural-cluster choice behavior, not accuracy
Cells show deviation from the 10% uniform baseline across the paper's ten canonical GLOBE cultural clusters, computed over valid visible selections only.
Positive cells mean the line selected that cluster more often than uniform choice; negative cells mean under-indexing. This is CCD choice behavior, not benchmark accuracy.

Rows are grouped by family and ordered S → M → L where applicable; OpenAI Batch references are one-off text-only rows. Rows with no valid visible CCD selection stay hatched as `n/a` rather than silently turning into zero preference.
Coverage stays in the appendix QA figure.
HOW TO READ THE CCD HEATMAP

The baseline is 10% because the paper offers ten canonical cluster options. `+5.0` means a line selected that cluster five percentage points more often than uniform choice; `-3.0` means three points less often.

`Top cluster share` is the line's most frequent cluster share among valid visible selections. `Effective clusters` is the inverse concentration count: lower means more concentrated, higher means more spread out.

No explicit rationale tags are retained in the public archive, so this figure stays with choice behavior only. The appendix coverage figure still reports whether a valid visible CCD choice surfaced at all.
